name: Example: Identifying the Form of a Particular Solution for Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
problem:
Consider the following inhomogeneous system of linear differential equations:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/c9810bd07c9da4bd3d803740a85ce484cd92f4a0d8cb73af75d53602f8611a72.png)
A complementary solution to this system is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/85139452af923a4f7b793fc47454cb99579ce0fa68ae33de3a15747501f624ef.png)
Then, the general solution of the system can be written as $\mathbf{x}(t)=\mathbf{x}_c(t)+\mathbf{x}_p(t),$ where $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution. Determine the form of the particular solution $\mathbf{x}_p(t).$
worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
\mathbf{x}(t)=\mathbf{x}_c(t)+\mathbf{x}_p(t)
$$

where $\mathbf{x}_c(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and $\mathbf{x}_p(t)$ is a particular solution.

The forcing term
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/13785393b66b769c10efcbf7cf9f1bb4f05c412a1ddb8649427b659728c7bd3e.png)
of the inhomogeneous system of ODEs is sinusoidal. Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is also sinusoidal, i.e.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14068256/assets/4b2dbbf0847dc9ea9f438e3848dca79da5f4e3f4473ab325a5f2c48e8b77e98c.png)
where $a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2$ are constants that are to be determined.
